evaluations.label: A
errors: Action item owner written as 'Dirk Mengveld'; the transcript has him introduce himself as 'Dirk Meinfeld'.

'The interface designer urged familiarity and rational changes' - the transcript says 'No rational changes or whatever, 'cause it revolutionary changes', i.e. he argued against big changes, not for 'rational changes'.
The User Interface Designer is never named even though he introduced himself as Nick Broer.
strengths: Nearly every claim traces to the transcript, with who-said-what kept straight (Mark confirmed TV-only scope, Xavier raised light material, UI designer raised accessibility and the tight margin).

Captures the key numbers (EUR 25 selling price, ~EUR 12.50 production), the scope decision, the three-phase plan, the project folder, the personal coach giving assignments, and the 30-minute reconvene.
Records that Dirk had no marketing ideas ready yet, and turns that into the one action item that is actually supported by the transcript.
Clear sectioning with timestamps, readable by someone who missed the meeting.
weaknesses: Omits Xavier's three industrial-design questions (what happens inside, what it is made of, what it should look like).
Spends a lot of space on the animal-drawing warmup relative to its importance.
Only one action item; does not spell out that each person goes off to do individual work before the next meeting as an assignment for everyone.

evaluations.label: B
errors: 'Mark Knopp' - the project manager only gave his first name, Mark; the surname is invented.
'Xavier Juukens' and 'Dirk Mankveld' - the transcript has Xavier Juergens and Dirk Meinfeld.
Action item 'Provide personal assignments to team members' assigned to Mark; the transcript says the personal coach will give the assignments.

Action items 'Prepare intuitive design concepts' (UI designer) and 'Address material considerations for lightweight design' (Xavier) were never assigned in the meeting; they are inferred from remarks.
'Dolphin: freedom, smooth design' - nothing about smooth design was said of the dolphin; 'looks smooth' was Mark's comment on the tiger drawing.
'30-minute break before next meeting' - it is 30 minutes of individual work with assignments, not a break.
Timestamp (13:53) for an action item is after the meeting ended at 13:42; (10:34) for scope clarification is wrong (it happened around 11:25-11:34).
strengths: Covers all the main topics in order: project goals, three phases, whiteboard, animal metaphors, scope, usability, light material, price points, next steps.
Correct numbers (EUR 25 and ~EUR 12.5) and correct scope decision (TV only, no multi-device).
Attempts per-person action items with owners.
weaknesses: Telegraphic fragments with almost no attribution of who said or decided what.
Most of the action items are invented or misassigned, which is the one place a reader would act on these notes.
Several name transcription errors and an invented surname.
Does not mention that the marketing expert has no findings yet, or Xavier's three questions.

evaluations.label: C
errors: 'Mark Knopf: project manager' - the surname is not in the transcript; Mark gave only his first name.
'Dirk Mengveld' and 'Xavier Jökens' - the transcript has Dirk Meinfeld and Xavier Juergens.
'UI designer also present (name not captured)' - he introduced himself as Nick Broer.
'Intuitive design: stick to what users are familiar with, rational changes only' - the transcript says 'No rational changes or whatever', so 'rational changes only' reverses the garbled wording.
'Dolphin: freedom, openness' - 'openness' was not said; he mentioned freedom, the ocean and swimming.
strengths: Compact and well organized; a reader gets the project, the goals, the prices, the scope decision and the next step in under a minute.
Only set of notes to record Xavier's three industrial-design questions.
Correct on the key facts: TV-only scope, EUR 25 / ~EUR 12.50, three phases with functional design first, personal coach giving assignments, 30-minute reconvene, lightweight material.
The 'distinct and stand out from competitors' takeaway is supported by Mark's closing remark.
weaknesses: No action items section and no owners; a reader does not learn that Dirk still owes marketing input.
Design considerations are listed without saying who raised them (UI designer raised scope and accessibility, Xavier raised material, Mark confirmed TV-only).
Invented surname for the project manager and mangled names for two others.
Omits the whiteboard responsiveness complaint and Mark's note that accessibility for seriously disabled users 'might be a problem'.

evaluations.label: D
errors: 'kick off TS3012a' - no project code was mentioned anywhere in the transcript; this is invented.
'Markoff' - the project manager's name is Mark.
'Savier' / 'Savier Jokins' and 'Dirk Mangfelt' - the transcript has Xavier Juergens and Dirk Meinfeld.
'Speaker 4 acts as the User Interface Designer' - he introduced himself as Nick Broer.
'Speaker 4 clarifies that the scope of the project is limited to a TV remote control' - the UI designer asked the question; Mark clarified that the project is TV-only.
Open Design Questions lists 'Should the device be designed as a multi-remote control or limited strictly to television functions?' - this was settled in the meeting (TV only), not left open.
'Savier Jokins suggests using lightweight materials that are aesthetically impactful' - he only said the material should be light; 'aesthetically impactful' is invented.
Both action items are unowned and were not assigned in the meeting; they are rewritten from the project brief and role descriptions.
strengths: Prose summary plus outline gives a readable narrative of the meeting flow.
Correct prices (25 euros selling, ~12.50 production), correct three-phase plan, correct roles and role descriptions, correct 30-minute reconvene.
Captures the accessibility question and the light-material point.
weaknesses: The most name errors of the four plus an invented project code, which undermines trust in everything else.
Lists a decided item (TV-only scope) as an open question, and misattributes the clarification.
Action items are generic restatements of the brief with no owner and no link to anything said.
Summary and Outline sections repeat each other, so the notes are long without adding information; omits that the personal coach gives the assignments and that Dirk has no marketing input yet.

rationale: A is the most faithful to the transcript: attributions are right, the numbers and the TV-only scope decision are right, it records the personal coach, the 30-minute reconvene and the fact that Dirk owes marketing input, and its only slips are a mangled surname, one garbled phrase and the missing UI designer name. C is accurate and compact and is the only set to capture Xavier's three questions, but it invents a surname for Mark, mangles two others, gives no action items or owners and does not say who raised what. B covers the topics but in fragments, invents a surname, misassigns the personal-assignment task to Mark when the personal coach does it, invents two action items and has a timestamp after the meeting ended. D has the most fabrication (a project code, 'Markoff', 'Savier', 'aesthetically impactful'), lists the settled TV-only scope as an open question, misattributes that clarification to the UI designer and offers only generic unowned action items, so it ranks last despite its readable prose.
